The Future of Skilled Trades 👊

Many worry that robotics and AI will eliminate skilled trade jobs.
 
The reality points in a different direction.

The U.S. already faces major shortages: 
Projections show millions of unfilled positions by 2030. An aging workforce is retiring faster than new workers are entering the field, while demand continues to rise from infrastructure projects, clean energy, manufacturing, and especially the massive buildout of AI data centers.

Technology is changing how the work gets done, but it is not eliminating the need for skilled people. Robots and AI can handle repetitive or dangerous tasks, improve safety, and boost productivity. 

Core trades that require real-time judgment in unique environments, electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, and similar roles remain very difficult to fully automate.

I know this to be 100% true from my own time in the industry. We were already dealing with serious shortages of people who could do these trades and were willing to work a 40 hour week and the situation has only gotten worse.  On many job sites you would see entire framing crews made up of workers who couldn’t speak English. A lot of those workers are gone now, which is why the cost of finding reliable and qualified people had become outrageously expensive.  Deportation was something that needed to happen 💯, yet what was going to replace this work force?

This is exactly the need that new technology is helping to answer. The result is higher demand for workers who combine traditional craft skills with comfort around new tools. These hybrid roles are already seeing strong growth and solid pay potential, all while helping keep costs more manageable for both the consumer and the builder. Far from disappearing, skilled trades are evolving into higher-tech, higher-value careers that form the physical foundation of the digital and energy transitions.  Those who adapt will find more opportunity, better conditions, and greater freedom than before. The new revolution isn’t about replacing skilled hands, it’s about amplifying what they can achieve.

Its price rose more than 50% from around $814 on Sep. 4 and briefly entered the $1,249–$1,257 area before buyers lost momentum. The breakout also placed Zcash above $1,000 for the first time in years. Price continued to hold more than $200 above the psychological level at the time of writing, even as Bitcoin and Ethereum faced broader selling pressure.

⚡️ Derivatives liquidations contributed to the initial acceleration. More than $34.5 million in ZEC short positions were reportedly closed during a 24-hour period as bearish traders were forced to buy back the asset. Short liquidations accounted for about 94% of the total cited liquidations. Forced buying helped ZEC clear resistance quickly, but the same leverage that drove the advance could increase volatility if traders begin taking profits.
